comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's current programme pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC joint degree with Leiden University centred on the living cell and on applying chemistry, biology, physics, mathematics, bioinformatics and pharmacology to biotechnology and health. The official curriculum chart linked by the current programme page is dated September 2026. It accounts for the complete 180 EC and is reproduced below at its exact printed component-credit level; Dutch component titles are translated into English.

alternatives.concept: A related-fields response centred on molecular cell biology, biochemistry, one life-science laboratory course, genetics, immunity, pharmacology and disease, combined with research methods, calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, programming, data science and image analysis. Life-cycle assessment and ethics add sustainable and societal context. It does not reproduce the external degree's organic/chemical biology, thermodynamics, transport, microbial-process engineering, biocatalysis, advanced biotechnology laboratories or 20-EC biotechnology project.

The label reflects those supported strands and avoids claiming the absent chemistry and bioprocess-engineering curriculum.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes every dependent life-science and biomedical course. Mathematical Methods precedes calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods and probability; Introduction to Programming precedes Algorithms & Data Structures. Biochemistry and physiology precede later molecular pathology, pharmacology and mechanisms of disease, while research and statistical foundations precede advanced data analysis. Every course is offered in its assigned term, and the schedule contains 24 unique courses, four per semester, Year-1 PPD and six 300-level courses.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The complete related-fields alternative already combines the target's molecular/cellular, laboratory, quantitative, medical, sustainable and societal strands as far as UCR allows. The remaining generator row joins medical and sustainable biotechnology in one application statement; its medical content is covered through pharmacology, immunity, disease and genetics, while its sustainability content is covered through life-cycle assessment and ethics. Splitting those applications into a second programme would either repeat the same molecular/quantitative core or drop the very biotechnology and process-engineering content UCR lacks, so it does not yield a genuinely different defensible 24-course route. Production stops at one alternative.

notes.text: The UCR programme combines molecular and biomedical life science, one broad laboratory course, genetics, immunity, disease, research methods, mathematics, programming and data analysis, with limited sustainability and ethics context. It does not reproduce Life Science and Technology's organic and chemical biology, structural biology, thermodynamics, transport, microbial physiology, biocatalysis, bioprocess modelling, biotechnology process design, staged practical training or 20-EC biotechnology project.
